s0001: Know how the degree of grinding (particle size) of a substance affects how fast it dissolves in water, and choose the correct conclusion and its reason
s0002: Find which substance is in smaller pieces: small particles touch the water on more sides, so they dissolve faster. Check both the answer and the reason.
s0003:
Malika poured the same amount of warm water into two identical glasses. She put one sugar cube in Glass 1 and the same weight of granulated sugar in Glass 2, and stirred both in the same way (see the picture).
Which statement is correct, and why?
s0008: The sugar cube dissolves faster, because it is heavier and sinks into the water faster.
s0009: Both dissolve in the same time, because they have the same weight.
s0010: The granulated sugar dissolves faster, because it is made of tiny grains and more of it touches the water.
s0011: The granulated sugar dissolves faster, because granulated sugar is sweeter than a sugar cube.
s0013: In both glasses the water, the amount of sugar, and the stirring are the same. Only one thing is different.
s0014: Difference: cube — large, granulated sugar — tiny grains
s0015: The difference is the size of the sugar: one is a single large cube, and the other is tiny grains.
s0016: Tiny grains → touch more water → dissolve fast
s0017: The water surrounds the tiny grains on all sides, so they dissolve faster.
s0018: Answer: C) The granulated sugar dissolves faster
s0019: So the correct answer is C: the granulated sugar dissolves faster because it is in tiny grains.
s0020: A student who chose A thought a large, heavy piece dissolves faster; in fact, only the surface of a large piece touches the water, and the inside stays undissolved for a long time.
s0021: A student who chose B looked only at the weight and did not consider that the size of the pieces affects how fast they dissolve.
s0022: A student who chose D correctly knew that the granulated sugar dissolves faster but gave the wrong reason: sweetness does not determine how fast something dissolves.
s0023: Find what is the same and what is different in the two glasses.

Jasur poured the same amount of cold water into two identical glasses. He put a spoonful of fine table salt in Glass 1 and a large lump of rock salt of the same weight in Glass 2, and stirred both in the same way (see the picture).
Which statement is correct, and why?
s0027: The fine salt dissolves faster, because its particles are small and the water quickly surrounds them on all sides.
s0028: The rock salt dissolves faster, because it is large and takes up more of the water.
s0029: Both dissolve in the same time, because both are table salt.
s0030: The fine salt dissolves faster, because it looks whiter and lighter.
s0031: Same type of salt, same weight, same water
s0032: Both glasses have the same salt and the same water. The only difference is the size of the salt particles.
s0033: Glass 1: tiny particles;  Glass 2: one large lump
s0034: The salt in the first glass is fine, and in the second it is one large lump.
s0035: Tiny particles → touch more water → dissolve fast
s0036: Water touches each of the tiny particles, but only the outside of the large lump touches the water.
s0037: Answer: A) The fine salt dissolves faster
s0038: So the correct answer is A.
s0039: A student who chose B thought a large lump dissolves faster; in fact, the inside of a large lump does not touch the water and dissolves slowly.
s0040: A student who chose C thought that if the substance is the same, the dissolving time is the same too, and did not consider particle size.
s0041: A student who chose D correctly found which dissolves faster but gave the wrong reason: color does not affect how fast something dissolves.
s0042: Think about which salt the water can touch in more places at the same time.
s0043: Know that metals conduct heat well while wood and plastic conduct it poorly, and use this to explain an everyday event
s0044: Think about which object is touching something hot and which material heat passes through more easily. Do not confuse conducting heat with conducting electricity.
s0045:
At a teahouse, Nilufar put an aluminum spoon and a plastic spoon into hot tea. A few minutes later, the handle of the aluminum spoon was hotter than the handle of the plastic spoon.
What is the reason for this?
s0046: Aluminum is always hotter than plastic.
s0047: Aluminum conducts heat better than plastic.
s0048: Aluminum conducts electricity better than plastic.
s0049: The aluminum spoon heats the tea faster than the plastic spoon.
s0050: Both spoons are in hot tea
s0051: Both spoons are standing in the same hot tea.
s0053: Heat moves from the tea all the way to the handle of the spoon.
s0054: Metal (aluminum) — conducts heat well; plastic — poorly
s0055: Metal conducts heat well, and plastic conducts it poorly. That is why the aluminum handle heats up quickly.
s0056: Answer: B) Aluminum conducts heat better
s0057: So the correct answer is B.
s0058: A student who chose A thought metal is hot by itself; in fact, at room temperature both spoons are equally warm.
s0059: A student who chose C confused electric current with heat: there is no current here; the question is about heat.
s0060: A student who chose D mixed up cause and effect: the spoon does not heat the tea; the tea heats the spoon.

s0192: Know that objects fall to the ground because of the Earth's pull (gravity)
s0193: If nothing is holding an object, the Earth pulls it toward itself — this is gravity. Other forces (magnetism, air resistance, pushing) do not make an object fall down.

s0198: A push from the tree branch
s0199: The apple came off the branch → nothing holds it
s0200: Once the apple comes off the branch, nothing holds it up.
s0201: The Earth pulls all objects toward itself
s0202: The Earth pulls all objects toward itself. This force is called gravity.
s0203: Air resistance — slows the fall, does not cause it
s0204: The air slows the apple's fall a little, but it does not pull it down.
